subject: What do you call God when you pray?
preview: Every name He revealed came at the exact moment someone needed it.
linkText: The Names of God and What They Mean

blocks.text: Most of us pray to "God" or "Lord" and never think twice about it.
It is just what we have always called Him.
But in Scripture, a name is not just a label.
It is a claim about who someone actually is.
And God is called by a lot of names.
Each one showed up in a real moment, when someone needed to know something true about Him.
🔹 El Shaddai: God Almighty, for Abram at ninety nine, still waiting on a son.
🔹 El Elyon: God Most High, for Abram walking off a battlefield.
🔹 El Roi: the God who sees, for Hagar alone in the wilderness.
🔹 Jehovah Shalom: the LORD is peace, for a frightened Gideon.
Think about Hagar for a second.
She was a pregnant servant girl, cast out, running alone into the wilderness.
Nobody was coming for her.
But God found her first, and she gave Him a name. "Thou God seest me."
It is the only name in the Bible that a woman gives to God, and she gave it in the loneliest moment of her life.
Here is what I want you to understand.
Every name of God is Him answering a question His people were actually asking.
Can You keep an impossible promise? Do You see me? Are You angry with me?
Whatever you are asking Him right now, He has already answered someone who asked it before you.
And there is one detail most name lists get wrong.
Jehovah Jireh was not a name God announced over Himself. Abraham named the mountain that after God provided the ram.
That does not make it less true. It just means the real verses are even better than the graphic.
In the full guide I walk through Elohim, Yahweh, El Shaddai, El Elyon, El Roi, Adonai and the Jehovah names, with the exact verse where each one appears.
